Theoretical investigations of #P have led to the discovery of deep connections in complexity theory (Toda 1989; Valiant 1979), and there is strong evidence for its hardness (Arora and Barak 2009). This technique guarantees a low expected number of collisions, even for an arbitrary distribution of the data being hashed. We have shown that universal hashing enables us to partition the set ...
section_summaries.conclusion: Constrained sampling and counting problems have a wide range of applications in artificial intelligence, verification, machine learning and the like. DIEJOB then conducts label propagation to find mentions that can be confidently used as training examples to train classifiers for labeling new entity mentions. An argument usually consists of a central claim (or conclusion) and several supporting premises. Constructing arguments of high quality would require the inclusion of diverse information, such as factual evidence and solid reasoning (Rieke et al., 1997; Park and Cardie, 2014). For instance, as shown in Figure 1, the editor on idebate.org – a Wikipedia-style website for gathering pro and con arguments on controversial issues, utilizes arguments based on study, factual evidence, and expert opinion to support the anti-gun claim ...

Existing work focuses on argument extraction from news articles, legal documents, or online comments without given userspecified claim (Moens et al., 2007; Palau and Moens, 2009; Mochales and Moens, 2011; Park and Cardie, 2014). Argument scheme classification is also widely studied (Biran and Rambow, 2011; Feng and Hirst, 2011; Rooney et al., 2012; Stab and Gurevych, 2014; Al Khatib et al., 2016), which emphasizes on distinguishing different types of arguments. To the best of our ...
section_summaries.conclusion: We presented a novel study on the task of sentence-level supporting argument detection from relevant documents for a user-specified claim. Based on our newly-collected dataset, we characterized arguments of different types with a rich feature set. We also showed that leveraging argument type information can further improve the performance of supporting argument detection.

section_summaries.conclusion: We propose a multimodal Recurrent Neural Network (m-RNN) framework that performs at the state-of-the-art in three tasks: sentence generation, sentence retrieval given query image and image retrieval given query sentence. Our m-RNN is powerful of connecting images and sentences and is flexible to incorporate more complex image representations and more sophisticated language models.

section_summaries.introduction: This paper studies the fundamental problem of learning and inference in the generator network (Goodfellow et al., 2014), which is a generative model that has become popular recently. section_summaries.methodology: We venture to propose that a main advantage of a generative model is to learn from incomplete or indirect data, which are not uncommon in practice. Learning the generator network from incomplete data can be considered a non-linear generalization of matrix completion. We also propose to evaluate the learned generator network by the reconstruction error on the testing data.

section_summaries.introduction: In machine learning and statistics, empirical risk minimization (ERM) is a dominant inference technique, wherein a model is chosen which minimizes some loss function over a data set. As the choice of loss function used in ERM may have a large impact on the model chosen, how should one choose this loss? A growing body of work in property elicitation seeks to answer this question, by viewing a loss function as “incentivizing” the prediction of a particular conditional statistic (Lambert et al., 2008; Gneiting, 2011; Steinwart et al., 2014; Frongillo ...
section_summaries.related_work: Our work is inspired in part by Frongillo et al. (2015) which proposes a way to elicit the confidence (inverse of variance) of an agent’s estimate of the bias of a coin by simply flipping it twice. In our terminology, this follows from the fact that the variance is (1, 2)-elicitable. Multi-observation losses have been previously introduced to learn embeddings (Hadsell et al., 2006; Schroff et al., 2015; Ustinova and Lempitsky, 2016), though an explicit property/statistic is never discussed.
section_summaries.conclusion: An immediate host of directions is the proving of upper and lower bounds on elicitation frontiers for various properties. Another direction is to formalize learning guarantees for multi-observation regression under suitable assumptions on slow-changing conditional distributions.
